units.sourceHTML: These tests are mainly useful with ranges (‘+n’ and ‘-n’).

units.text: True if the file was last accessed (or its status changed, or it was modified) ⟦0⟧*24 hours ago. The number of 24-hour periods since the file’s timestamp is always rounded down; therefore 0 means “less than 24 hours ago”, 1 means “between 24 and 48 hours ago”, and so forth. Fractional values are supported but this only really makes sense for the case where ranges (‘⟦1⟧’ and ‘⟦2⟧’) are used.
units.sourceHTML: True if the file was last accessed (or its status changed, or it was modified) n*24 hours ago. The number of 24-hour periods since the file’s timestamp is always rounded down; therefore 0 means “less than 24 hours ago”, 1 means “between 24 and 48 hours ago”, and so forth. Fractional values are supported but this only really makes sense for the case where ranges (‘+n’ and ‘-n’) are used.

units.text: True if the file was last accessed (or its status changed, or it was modified) ⟦0⟧ minutes ago. units.text: The ‘⟦0⟧’ option is unlike most other options in that it has an effect on the way that other tests are performed. The affected tests are ‘⟦1⟧’, ‘⟦2⟧’, ‘⟦3⟧’, ‘⟦4⟧’, ‘⟦5⟧’ and ‘⟦6⟧’. The ‘⟦7⟧’ option only affects the behaviour of any tests which appear after it on the command line.
units.sourceHTML: The ‘-daystart’ option is unlike most other options in that it has an effect on the way that other tests are performed. The affected tests are ‘-amin’, ‘-cmin’, ‘-mmin’, ‘-atime’, ‘-ctime’ and ‘-mtime’. The ‘-daystart’ option only affects the behaviour of any tests which appear after it on the command line.
